t: the boone county health department is the fiscal sponsor for the boone county quick response team (qrt). this funding will be used to purchase food, hygiene, household, and clothing items, seasonal items, and temporary shelter items for qrt clients. the qrt will host weekly yoga classes and weekly celebrate recovery meetings for individuals in recovery. funds will be used for a meal that participants will share before recovery meeting instruction. in addition, the health department will purchase two automated external defibrillators for its facility. west virginia university research corporation is the fiscal sponsor for this project. west virginia university's school of public health (wvuph) will launch the mind the bump research project, which will test a prenatal eating behaviors screening tool that identifies eating disorders in pregnant women. the tool will be tested in clinical settings across the foundation's region. wvuph will recruit clinicians and provide marketing materials with a qr code for participants to take a brief questionnaire. women who complete the questionnaire will receive a $10 gift card and be asked to participate in a zoom interview. women who complete the interview will be compensated with a $40 gift card. ymca will utilize funding to support a portion of salary costs for the new youth program coordinator position, as well as food and supplies for youth programs offered at the phil cline family ymca. funds also will enable the ymca to continue providing swim lessons to approximately 50 low-income, at-risk, and minority youth who may not otherwise be able to access swim instruction. the logan county child advocacy center will use funding to support a portion of the annual salary, fringe benefit, and travel expenses for its children's therapist, who will utilize the trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy model to work with children and their caregivers to address and process traumatic memories. ebenezer medical outreach (emo) in huntington, wv, will partner with marshall eye surgeons to establish a new clinic that will provide screening and follow-up care for diabetic retinopathy. emo will purchase ai-assisted retinal imaging technology that will enable its existing support staff to complete diabetic patients' recommended diabetic retinopathy eye screenings within the primary care setting. patients who screen positive for possible diabetic retinopathy will be referred to a new student-led comprehensive ophthalmological clinic hosted by marshall eye surgeons. emo also will purchase innovative vision kits designed to provide economical, same-day vision correction for community members with limited access to traditional eye care. facing hunger food bank will purchase fresh produce for individuals impacted by the february 2025 flooding in mingo county, wv and martin and pike counties in ky. funds also will be used for staff overtime and fuel costs associated with after hours and
